experiment: Batch up to four transient live-queue deliveries under one state-lock critical section in flushSlotLockedMode, then write them outside the lock.
motivation: The balanced QoS 1 profile showed flushSlotLockedMode at 20.36% self and 44.48% children, with sync.Futex.wait at 7.60%; the loop took the global state lock once per delivery.
implementation: Popped up to four QoS 0/1 deliveries per lock section; QoS 2 and durable Sessions stayed one-at-a-time.
Added a 4-KiB payload budget so 4-KiB messages kept one-at-a-time behavior.
Reserved route slots for the batch so concurrent publishers could not refill the queue and prevent push-back.
Deferred reservation release to the next loop iteration and marked the per-delivery helper inline.
conclusions: QoS 1 improved the targeted balanced shape (p50 3.623 -> 3.275 ms, p99 10.639 -> 7.833 ms) and serial throughput (57,246 -> 61,667/s), with other QoS 1 shapes roughly neutral.

QoS 2 regressed in four of five shapes even after restricting QoS 2 to one-at-a-time and inlining the helper: serial 27,398 -> 27,048/s with p99 0.042 -> 0.083 ms, publishers-32 38,309 -> 34,993/s, fanout-32 3,100 -> 2,808/s, balanced 3,212 -> 2,901/s.
The shared flush-path refactor and reservation accounting therefore cost more than the lock savings for QoS 2. The code change was reverted; no source change remains.
A future attempt must leave the QoS 2 flush path structurally unchanged, for example by batching only in a separate QoS 0/1-only writer or by removing the extra reservation/lock bookkeeping.
